cells.tense: The standard is being held steady in the hand, and the next piece can be shaped without hurry.
cells.act: commit to the long build and do today's part
cells.ask: Pick a goal you mean to finish and do today's single piece of it — the part where you can tell whether it is good yet. Nothing past that piece. The rest keeps.
cells.core:
You can tell a piece that works from one that only looks like it, and that difference is what you steer by. The build doesn't need to be flawless; it needs the next honest pass, and you make it without ceremony. That is why the direction stays clean instead of turning into motion that looks busy and finishes nothing.

Let today's part stay small. Name the thing you mean to finish, do the piece that can be done now, then stop before the plan grows. The refining is the work itself, not a mood that has to arrive first. Do it on the flat days the same as the charged ones, and momentum stops depending on how you feel.
cells.sheetLine: Today's piece, done honestly, is the whole job.
cells.verb: holding a private standard steady under the hand while the shape is refined
cells.place: the stretch of a goal where the direction has to be kept through resistance

cells.tense: The careful distinguishing is being spent on a version of the goal that hasn't happened yet.
cells.act: let what you gave up be seen by the people it was for, without a word about it
cells.ask: Show someone a piece you made, where they can see it — the piece itself, not the hours. If they remark on what it must have taken, don't explain and don't wave it off. Stay put.
cells.core:
The discernment is real and it is running past the work. Every unbuilt version gets weighed until it either shrinks or grows teeth, and more time goes into the argument than into the doing. The focus is still in the body, but the aim has moved beyond where you actually stand, so the push starts feeding on itself.

Bring an unseen piece out where the person it was for can see it. No report, no defense of the effort, just the thing. When someone acknowledges what it cost, let that land in you rather than stepping around it. The pressure leaves the careful thinking and goes back into the work where it belongs.
cells.sheetLine: Let the thing you made be seen before you've explained it.

cells.tense: The standard is still being measured carefully, but the motion it used to carry is gone.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: Take an offer that's already been made to you, at face value. Give something back at its true size. Something small, either direction. Leave the exchange open instead of closing it.
cells.core:
The perception runs with no target in it. The care that used to sort what matters from what doesn't still works, but there's nothing in front of it now — no goal you're actually moving toward — so the refining happens in place, and some days against yourself. The direction is paused, and the pause reads from inside as not wanting anything.

Keep a small exchange moving with someone instead. Take what's offered without first working out what you owe for it, and return something at its real size. Fairness here isn't a ledger; it's both directions staying open so neither side closes. When that back-and-forth moves again, motion comes back into the standard you hold.
cells.sheetLine: You're still measuring. There's just nothing under the hand.

cells.tense: What reads as ordinary follow-through is a discipline you've been running the whole time.
cells.act: walk through the thing you built and touch nothing
cells.ask: Go stand with something you finished. No sharpening, no next pass. Give it the look you'd give if somebody else had made it, and don't touch a thing while you're there.
cells.core:
There's a mind in this that can take a thing apart and put it back sharper, and you don't often call it yours. In your own telling it sounds like common sense, the way anyone would do it. So the refining happens and the eye doing the refining goes unnamed, which is fine until you stop believing the eye is there.

Stand with something you already made and leave the version alone. If the pull to improve one more corner rises, notice it and hold off — for this one visit. What's already made holds up under a plain look. Taking the satisfaction of it isn't laziness; it's the part of the build you keep skipping.
cells.sheetLine: The eye that shaped it is yours, not common sense.

attempts.check: The record supports the person holding a Habit (the Bound signature) in Drive, but it gives me no history of why Drive might be spent, no proof of past cost, and no evidence about a specific audience or team around them. A reader could reasonably say 'the goal isn't the problem, I have plenty of drive' — so the Too Much and Too Little cores are written as shapes of one moment they could name, not as claims about their life. The ask survives a wrong read because it is small, visible, and chosen by them anyway; the sentence that serves me more than them is any line implying they built something alone and disowned it, which I have kept out of the Unacknowledged core. The Diagonals in both directions are still the partner's own act — a daily return to the work, and a completion honored by others — so the medicine stays useful even if my read of the seat is off.

attempts.check: The record gives me a Bound Habit — a private standard refined through careful attention — seated in Drive, and nothing about who is around the person, what they gave up, or how long a pause has lasted. A reader could fairly say the drive is fine and the goal isn't the problem, so both failure statuses are written as two shapes of one moment they could recognise, neither given a cause. The asks vary in shape on purpose — a single piece, an outing to show, an open exchange, a plain visit — and each stays useful even if my read of the seat is off. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line that names their discipline for them; I have left it unnamed.
